profile.summary: Caduceus is a family of DNA language models for long human genomic sequences. It reads DNA one base at a time, looking both upstream and downstream, and is built so that a sequence and its reverse complement are treated consistently. The pretrained models output masked-base predictions and per-base embeddings that can be fine-tuned or used as features, for example for variant effect prediction.
profile.summary_source_locator: arXiv abstract; model card: Model Details; README: eQTL SNP Variant Effect Prediction

summary_quotes.text: the first family of RC equivariant bi-directional long-range DNA language models
the need to model long-range token interactions, the effects of upstream and downstream regions of the genome, and the reverse complementarity (RC) of DNA
This model was pre-trained on the human reference genome with sequence length 131,072 for 50k steps (each step contained ~1M base pairs / tokens).
For this task we fit a model to the pre-trained and frozen embeddings of the DNA language models.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Caduceus builds on the long-range Mamba block. The authors extend it to a BiMamba component that reads a sequence in both directions, and to a MambaDNA block that is also reverse-complement (RC) equivariant. The published checkpoints have hidden dimension 256 and 16 MambaDNA layers and were pretrained as masked language models on the human reference genome. In the RC-equivariant Caduceus-PS model the hidden state is twice the width of a non-equivariant model, and the card says to run a downstream model on the hidden state and its reverse complement, or average them, to get RC-invariant outputs.
sections.source_locator: arXiv abstract; model card: Model Details; README: Using Caduceus with Hugging Face

quotes.text: builds off the long-range Mamba block, and extends it to a BiMamba component that supports bi-directionality, and to a MambaDNA block that additionally supports RC equivariance
This is the Caduceus-PS model with hidden dimension 256 and 16 MambaDNA layers.
Note that the model hidden state will be **twice** that of a non-RC equivariant counterpart.
one can either run the downstream model on the hidden state and its RC or one can take the hidden state and its RC and average them before passing to the downstream model

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README lists two pretrained checkpoints on Hugging Face. Caduceus-Ph was trained with reverse-complement data augmentation. Caduceus-PS is RC equivariant by design and needs no augmentation. Both were trained on sequences of length 131k with model size 256 and 16 layers, for 50k steps at batch size 8. A result should name the checkpoint (Ph or PS) and its Hugging Face revision; this page read PS at revision d89eeb85 and Ph at revision b0477522. The repository also holds the training code used to reproduce the paper's pretraining and fine-tuning experiments.

strengths.text: Reverse-complement handling is built into Caduceus-PS, so it needs no reverse-complement data augmentation during pretraining or fine-tuning.

quotes.text: This model is reverse complement (RC) equivariant and thus no RC data augmentation is required when training this model, either during pre-training or for downstream fine-tuning.

strengths.text: The models are small, at about 7.7 million parameters, and read 131k-base sequences at single-base resolution.

run_guide.summary: Set up the repository's conda environment at a pinned commit and load a pretrained Caduceus checkpoint from Hugging Face for masked language modelling.
prerequisites: conda, to build the environment from caduceus_env.yml.
The environment pins python=3.8, pytorch=2.2.0, pytorch-cuda=12.1, transformers==4.38.1 and mamba-ssm==1.2.0.post1. GPU type and memory are not stated in the sources read.
Code and weights are Apache-2.0 licensed. The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/kuleshov-group/caduceus.git
cd caduceus
git checkout --detach 0060a6d8079b6a040fc55d505e15972a327b70a6
steps.explanation: The README does not give a clone command; the clone, cd and checkout lines are added to get the repository at the commit this page was written from.
steps.source_locator: README: title and citation; repository URL

steps.title: Load a pretrained checkpoint
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer

# See the `Caduceus` collection page on the hub for list of available models.
model_name = "kuleshov-group/caduceus-ph_seqlen-131k_d_model-256_n_layer-16"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(model_name)
PY
steps.explanation: The README snippet, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the tokenizer and the Caduceus-Ph weights. For Caduceus-PS, use the model name kuleshov-group/caduceus-ps_seqlen-131k_d_model-256_n_layer-16 as in its model card.
steps.source_locator: README: Using Caduceus with Hugging Face; model card: Using Caduceus

outputs: A loaded tokenizer and masked language model in memory. The snippet prints nothing; the sources give no example of running it on a sequence.
